name: Remix Clawwa
description:
WHATSAPP AI AUTO-REPLY — MASTER ENGINEERING REBUILD

Bug Fixes, Architecture Improvements, AI Intelligence, Performance & Premium UI/UX

You are acting as a senior Android engineer, AI systems architect, Kotlin specialist, distributed-systems engineer, computer-vision engineer, and product designer.

Your task is to investigate, upgrade, and substantially improve my EXISTING WhatsApp AI Auto-Reply Android application.

This is an existing Kotlin-based Android application. Do not start a separate project or discard working components unnecessarily.

EXISTING PROJECT CONFIGURATION

- Platform: Android
- Programming language: Kotlin
- UI: Existing Android application; preserve its established architecture where practical.

.

- AI architecture: Multiple AI providers and models.
- Conversation memory: Independent per-contact and per-group memory.
- Reply behaviour: Automatic AI replies by default.
- Design direction: Premium iOS-inspired aesthetics combined with futuristic sci-fi elements.

CRITICAL: Begin by inspecting the actual project source code. Understand the existing architecture, identify the root causes of bugs, and determine which components can be improved or need restructuring.

Do not assume how WhatsApp Web is implemented. Identify whether the project uses WebView, browser automation, or another mechanism before modifying its integration.

---

1. GROUP CHAT INTELLIGENCE

Completely fix group conversation recognition and handling.

The AI must understand the difference between:

- Individual conversations.
- WhatsApp group conversations.
- Individual participants inside groups.
- Messages sent by different group participants.
- Messages directed at the AI.
- Messages directed at another participant.

Requirements:

1. Correctly identify whether the current conversation is a group or individual chat.
2. Extract sender identity and message ownership accurately.
3. Maintain independent conversation context for each group.
4. Identify which participant sent each message.
5. Understand references, replies, and ongoing discussions within groups.
6. Avoid accidentally replying privately when a response should go to the group, or replying to the group when the response should be private.
7. Respect group-chat permissions everywhere.

If group chatting is disabled and I ask the AI to interact with a group, it must recognize the restriction and tell me that group chatting needs to be enabled.

Group permissions must be enforced at the actual message-sending layer, not merely through prompts.

---

2. RELIABLE MESSAGE DETECTION AND HIGH-SPEED PROCESSING

Fix missed messages, especially when someone sends the first message in a conversation.

The application must:

- Reliably detect incoming WhatsApp messages.
- Correctly initialize conversations that have never been processed before.
- Avoid losing messages during initialization.
- Process multiple conversations concurrently.
- Maintain independent processing queues per conversation.
- Prevent one slow conversation from blocking all others.
- Reduce unnecessary AI requests and processing delays.
- Handle temporary network failures and provider timeouts.
- Resume recoverable jobs without producing duplicate replies.

Use proper asynchronous Kotlin architecture, structured concurrency, cancellation handling, and persistent job state where appropriate.

Implement a reliable message lifecycle:

"Detected → Parsed → Context Loaded → AI Processing → Validated → Sending → Confirmed"

Failed jobs must have identifiable states and controlled retry behaviour.

Messages must never silently disappear from the processing pipeline.

---

3. INTELLIGENT CONVERSATION CONTEXT ENGINE

Introduce an optional Conversation Context Mode.

When enabled, the AI should examine previous conversation messages before responding.

It must understand:

- Previous discussions.
- Important information.
- Personal preferences.
- Questions awaiting answers.
- Ongoing conversations.
- Previously shared images and documents where their content has been successfully extracted.
- Relevant conversation history.

Support two context strategies:

A. Recent Context

Read the configured number of most recent messages.

B. Summarized Context

Maintain or generate a consolidated summary containing important conversation information.

The application should avoid repeatedly processing historical messages that have already been analyzed.

Maintain separate memory for every contact and group.

Do not mix the memory of different conversations.

---

4. CONFIGURABLE RECENT MESSAGE READING — IMPORTANT

This is a core feature.

Introduce a configurable setting that determines how many recent messages the AI should examine whenever it generates a response.

For example:

- Read the latest 3 messages.
- Read the latest 5 messages.
- Read the latest 10 messages.
- Read the latest 20 messages.
- Use the conversation summary instead.
- Use recent messages together with the conversation summary.

The message limit must be configurable.

Provide:

- An optional global setting.
- Optional per-conversation overrides.
- An enable/disable toggle.
- Persistent settings.

When enabled, the selected number of messages must be respected.

When disabled, use the application's default context strategy.

Attachment understanding is mandatory

The message count must include ALL supported message types, not just text.

For example, if I configure the AI to read the latest 3 messages and those messages contain:

1. A text message.
2. A photograph.
3. A sticker.

The AI must process all three messages.

It must not ignore the photograph or sticker simply because they are not text.

Supported content should include:

- Text messages.
- Images and photographs.
- Screenshots.
- Stickers.
- Animated stickers where extraction is supported.
- PDFs.
- Documents.
- Voice notes.
- Audio attachments.
- Other supported file formats.

Each message must retain its original sender, timestamp, type, and ordering.

For unsupported formats, use an appropriate extraction method where possible.

Never pretend an attachment was understood if it was not successfully processed.

---

5. AI-TRIGGERED REPLY CONTROLS

IMPORTANT CLARIFICATION:

I do not want ordinary manual messaging buttons as the primary fallback mechanism.

I want controls that let me manually trigger the AI to respond.

Inside individual conversations, implement two clearly accessible actions.

A. Reply with AI Now

When pressed:

1. Retrieve the selected conversation.
2. Read the configured number of recent messages.
3. Retrieve that conversation's independent memory.
4. Process supported attachments, including images, stickers, documents, and audio.
5. Understand the conversation context.
6. Generate a suitable response.
7. Send the response to the correct WhatsApp conversation.
8. Update the conversation's processing state.

This must work even when automatic replying has failed, provided the underlying WhatsApp integration and AI provider are available.

B. Keep Replying

Allow me to trigger another AI response or continue responding in the selected conversation.

It must:

- Use the correct conversation.
- Respect the configured context settings.
- Respect group-chat permissions.
- Use the selected AI provider.
- Prevent duplicate replies.
- Never send messages to the wrong recipient.

Both controls must be functional, not decorative.

The AI should also be able to explain privately why it cannot perform an action.

---

6. MULTI-PROVIDER AI ROUTING

Maintain support for multiple AI providers.

Build or improve a centralized provider-management architecture.

Requirements:

- Support existing integrations.
- Support different model capabilities.
- Handle text-only and multimodal models appropriately.
- Detect whether a model supports image input, audio input, and other required capabilities.
- Handle provider-specific request formats.
- Validate model responses.
- Implement sensible timeout and retry policies.
- Support provider fallback when configured.
- Avoid sending unsupported attachment types to incompatible models.

The system must distinguish between model incompatibility, provider errors, malformed responses, and genuine AI limitations.

Do not assume all providers support the same capabilities.

---

7. IMAGE, STICKER, DOCUMENT AND MULTIMODAL INTELLIGENCE

Completely investigate and improve the existing attachment-processing pipeline.

Current problems include:

- Image processing is too slow.
- Some working vision models incorrectly refuse image-related requests.
- The AI sometimes claims it cannot see an image even when the image is available.
- Stickers and other attachments are not always processed correctly.

Fix these issues.

Implement:

- Efficient attachment retrieval.
- Image decoding and preprocessing.
- Appropriate resizing and compression.
- MIME-type detection.
- Vision-model capability detection.
- Correct image payload construction for each provider.
- OCR for text-heavy images.
- Appropriate sticker decoding.
- Document text extraction.
- Audio transcription when supported.
- Efficient caching of previously processed attachments.

Do not unnecessarily process the same attachment multiple times.

For example, when the latest three messages contain text, a photograph, and a sticker, the AI should receive meaningful representations of all three.

Do not automatically refuse image-related requests simply because one provider fails.

Try a compatible alternative when configured.

If processing genuinely fails, report the failure privately and preserve the original message for retry.

---

8. BUSINESS MODE

Introduce an optional Business Mode with useful business intelligence.

The mode should support:

- Professional communication.
- Customer relationship management.
- Lead identification.
- Customer intent detection.
- Sales assistance.
- Product recommendations.
- Customer inquiry handling.
- Appointment coordination.
- Follow-up suggestions.
- Customer conversation summaries.
- Business-specific memory.
- Professional response generation.

Where appropriate, classify conversations into categories such as:

- Potential customer.
- Existing customer.
- Sales inquiry.
- Support request.
- Follow-up required.
- Important opportunity.

Build an attractive, futuristic business dashboard.

All displayed information must originate from actual conversation data or configured business information.

Do not create fake analytics or simulated CRM functionality.

---

9. DUPLICATE MESSAGE PREVENTION AND DELIVERY RELIABILITY

Investigate why the AI sometimes sends identical responses multiple times.

Implement:

- Stable incoming message identifiers.
- Unique processing-job identifiers.
- Idempotency protection.
- Outgoing message tracking.
- Persistent send states.
- Duplicate detection.
- Controlled retries.
- Delivery confirmation where supported.
- Recovery after application restarts.

Never blindly retry a message whose sending status is uncertain.

If WhatsApp Web does not provide reliable delivery confirmation, distinguish between sent, confirmed, and unknown states rather than claiming certainty.

Ensure that one incoming message does not accidentally trigger multiple identical AI responses.

---

10. PREMIUM CHAT UI/UX REDESIGN

Completely improve the Chats experience.

Design direction:

Apple-inspired refinement + futuristic sci-fi aesthetics.

The application should feel like a premium messaging product rather than a generic Android utility.

Requirements:

- Beautiful conversation lists.
- Modern message bubbles.
- Elegant contact and group headers.
- Premium typography.
- Consistent spacing.
- Smooth transitions.
- Subtle animations.
- Excellent scrolling performance.
- Responsive layouts.
- Refined dark and light themes.
- Subtle haptic feedback where supported.
- Attractive loading and processing states.
- Clear message attachment previews.
- Properly positioned AI controls.

Avoid unnecessary interface elements.

Every button must have a clear purpose.

Preserve existing navigation and functionality unless a change is necessary.

The result should be visually impressive without sacrificing usability.

---

11. SUMMARIZATION ENGINE

Fix the existing Summarize feature.

Investigate the null errors and broken functionality.

Requirements:

- Correctly identify the selected conversation.
- Retrieve its relevant messages.
- Support empty conversations gracefully.
- Support attachments when their content is extractable.
- Generate meaningful summaries.
- Display summaries correctly.
- Maintain per-conversation summaries.
- Handle malformed AI responses.
- Prevent null pointer exceptions.

A summary should capture important discussions, decisions, questions, preferences, and unresolved matters.

---

12. APPLICATION-WIDE STABILITY AUDIT

Conduct a complete application audit.

Investigate and fix:

- Null pointer exceptions.
- Crashes.
- Broken buttons.
- Incorrect state management.
- Failed API requests.
- Concurrency issues.
- Duplicate message processing.
- Database inconsistencies.
- WhatsApp Web integration failures.
- Incorrect conversation identification.
- Memory retrieval errors.
- Attachment processing failures.
- UI responsiveness issues.
- Background processing failures.

Do not simply catch exceptions and ignore them.

Find and fix the underlying causes.

Use structured error reporting and meaningful private diagnostics.

Never expose API keys, credentials, or sensitive message content in logs.

---

13. SETTINGS AND CONFIGURATION

Provide a clean settings architecture.

Relevant optional settings should include:

- Automatic replying.
- Group chatting.
- Conversation Context Mode.
- Recent Message Reading.
- Configurable message count.
- Per-contact context overrides.
- Summarized Context Mode.
- Business Mode.
- AI provider selection.
- Model selection.
- Provider fallback.
- Attachment processing preferences.

Settings must persist across application restarts.

The interface should clearly distinguish global settings from per-conversation settings.

---

14. ENGINEERING AND IMPLEMENTATION RULES

1. Inspect the entire existing source code before making architectural changes.
2. Preserve working features.
3. Do not rewrite functional components without a clear engineering reason.
4. Use Kotlin best practices.
5. Maintain compatibility with the existing WhatsApp Web integration.
6. Use proper asynchronous processing.
7. Avoid blocking the Android main thread.
8. Protect against race conditions.
9. Optimize memory and CPU consumption.
10. Use persistent storage for recoverable processing states.
11. Implement real functionality, not mock interfaces.
12. Do not remove existing AI providers without justification.
13. Do not expose credentials.
14. Test all major workflows.
15. Build the application and resolve compilation errors.

---

15. REQUIRED TESTING

Before declaring completion, test:

- First-time incoming conversations.
- Existing conversations.
- Individual chats.
- Group chats.
- Different group participants.
- Group-chat disabled behaviour.
- Automatic replies.
- Reply with AI Now.
- Keep Replying.
- Different recent-message limits.
- Text-only conversations.
- Images and screenshots.
- Stickers.
- Documents.
- Voice messages.
- Multimodal provider compatibility.
- Conversation memory isolation.
- Summarization.
- Business Mode.
- Multiple simultaneous conversations.
- Duplicate-message prevention.
- Network interruptions.
- Application restarts.
- Provider failures.
- Empty conversations.

Add automated tests for core business logic and integration tests wherever practical.

Report actual test results. Never claim that a feature works simply because its UI was implemented.

---

FINAL OBJECTIVE

Transform the EXISTING application into a highly intelligent, reliable, fast, multimodal WhatsApp AI assistant.

The finished product should combine:

- Excellent conversation intelligence.
- Independent per-chat memory.
- Accurate group understanding.
- Reliable automatic replies.
- AI-triggered reply controls.
- Advanced attachment understanding.
- Multiple AI providers.
- Business intelligence.
- Robust message delivery.
- Exceptional visual design.

MOST IMPORTANT: Correctness and reliability come before visual appearance.

Do not stop after implementing the UI. Do not produce placeholder features. Do not hide errors.

Investigate the architecture, fix the actual problems, implement the complete functionality, build the application, test it, and provide a clear implementation and testing report.

The final result must be a genuinely working application.
